remainingBlockers.item: New rules are NOT deployed. The live project still runs the baseline rules, so SEC-01/02/03/09/12 remain exploitable in production until deployment.
Before deployment the real App Owner must receive the claim via scripts/admin/setAppOwner.ts (requires Admin credentials and a verified email), otherwise the owner loses access.
firebase.json deploys rules to the (default) database; the app uses named database ai-studio-37d17c3e-…. Multi-database deploy config required.
Commercial authority (plans, entitlements, subscriptions, payments) is still localStorage + simulated payment (Phases 5-7). Clients can still self-grant Pro locally.
?preview=true shows DRAFT/UNPUBLISHED entities to any visitor; publishing state is localStorage (Phase 8).
Unauthenticated visitors are served demoStore data; demo data still in production bundle (Phase 11).
No real environment separation; environmentConfig is cosmetic (Phase 12).
Webhook secret still in source (src/services/paymentProvider.ts:30) although no longer in the production bundle (Phase 6).

decisionsTaken: Individual tenant stored in a new tenants/{ind_<uid>} registry; users.companyId stays null so existing entitlement resolution is unchanged.
Registration enforced by Firestore rules on a single batch (server-side enforcement) rather than a Cloud Function, because backend implementation is deferred to Phase 5 by the directive.
App Owner via custom claims (not an owner registry document) to avoid extra get() calls in rules.
Demo-only switch uses Vite's import.meta.env.DEV until Phase 12 introduces full environment configuration.
Company invoices restricted to company admins; company subscription remains readable by all members (plan display).
DSBC emulator uses dedicated ports (hub 4480, logging 4580, firestore 8180, auth 9477) because another project's emulator suite occupies the defaults on this machine.
